{
  "correction_rules": [
    "Adjust forecasts downward when sentiment is negative (sentiment < 0) to counteract overconfidence in upward moves.",
    "Reduce forecast magnitude by 5-10% when sentiment is mildly negative (sentiment = 0.00) to account for potential mean reversion.",
    "Avoid sharp upward spikes in forecasts following recent price declines; apply a lagged smoothing filter to prevent overshoot.",
    "If true outcome is consistently below forecast (persistent underperformance), apply a downward bias correction by 3-5% for the next 3-5 days.",
    "When sentiment is positive (sentiment > 0), allow for slight upward bias but cap forecast growth at 2-3% above recent 7-day average to avoid overreaction.",
    "For long-term (30-day) forecasts, apply a mean-reversion correction if forecast deviates > 1.5σ from 30-day historical mean.",
    "If forecast is significantly higher than true outcome (e.g., > 10% over), reduce by 10-15% and re-estimate based on sentiment trend.",
    "When sentiment is rising (e.g., 0.50 or higher), increase forecast volatility slightly to reflect heightened market uncertainty."
  ]
}
